title: 2124-moment-family-open-time-series-foundation
universal_lens: MOMENT unifies temporal dynamics via a channel-independent, patch-based masked autoencoder. By applying reversible instance normalization and reconstructing stochastically masked segments, the encoder extracts scale-invariant geometric priors from raw time-series manifolds, establishing a universal latent representation for sequential data.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps MOMENT's reconstruction errors to conformal prediction sets. The frozen encoder yields high-dimensional embeddings of team/player trajectories; Bayesian linear probing on these embeddings quantifies epistemic uncertainty, while calibration lanes adjust for regime shifts in sports performance metrics.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the patched transformer as a situational state-transition engine. Channel independence forces downstream heads to explicitly learn cross-channel (e.g., offensive/defensive) correlations. Fixed-length interpolation aligns discrete game events into continuous latent spaces for real-time tactical inference.

primitives.name: Reversible Instance Normalization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - RevIN normalization: x̃ = (x - μ)/σ per instance, reversible at output.

primitives.assumptions: Stationary statistics within the local context window; non-zero variance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when \sigma \to 0 (constant series), causing numerical instability.

primitives.name: Masked Patch Reconstruction Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Masked pretraining loss: MSE over masked patches only, L = (1/|M|)Σ_{j∈M} ||ŷ_j - y_j||2.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L: reconstruction loss (dimensionless), |M|: number of masked patches (integer), \hat{y}_j: predicted patch vector (dimensionless), y_j: ground truth patch vector (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Temporal continuity allows contextual inference of missing segments; MSE is an appropriate fidelity metric.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under highly stochastic, non-Markovian noise where local context provides zero mutual information about masked patches.

reasoning_traces.think:
The MOMENT architecture fundamentally re-parameterizes time-series analysis by treating temporal sequences as bags of fixed-length patches, analogous to natural language processing tokens. The core mathematical operator is the Reversible Instance Normalization (RevIN), which decouples intra-series distribution shifts from inter-series structural dependencies. By normalizing each instance independently, the model learns invariant geometric features of the underlying dynamical system. The masked patch reconstruction objective then acts as a powerful regularizer, forcing the encoder to internalize long-range temporal dependencies to accurately predict missing segments. In the context of Galaxy Sports Engine (GSE), this translates to a robust foundation model capable of generalizing across diverse sports metrics (e.g., NFL play-by-play, NBA tracking data). However, the strict channel-independence assumption implies that multivariate correlations (e.g., between offense and defense) are not captured during pretraining but must be re-learned by task-specific heads. This creates a dual-layer architecture: a universal temporal backbone and specialized situational reasoning modules. The fixed input length of 512 necessitates interpolation for shorter series, introducing potential artifacts if the sampling rate does not align with the intrinsic timescale of the sport. Ultimately, the masked autoencoder framework provides a mathematically sound basis for unsupervised feature extraction, enabling transfer learning to downstream tasks like spread forecasting and anomaly detection without requiring massive labeled datasets.
